reportTitle: Sabit Financial Close Engine - Final Technical QA Report

check_1_backend_tsc.details: Compilation completed with zero errors. No output from tsc --noEmit indicates clean pass.

check_2_frontend_nextjs_build.details: Build compiled successfully. 43 routes generated (19 static, 24 dynamic). No warnings or errors. Next.js 14.2.3.

check_3_backend_tests.details: No 'test' script defined in package.json. Only 'test:integration' and 'test:integration:dev' exist. No unit test framework (jest, vitest, mocha) is in devDependencies. Unit test coverage is absent.
check_3_backend_tests.recommendation: Add a unit test framework and define a 'test' script. Critical paths (certification, JE posting, statement generation) need unit tests.

check_5_migration_count.details: 163 migration files found in migrations/ directory.

check_6_conflicting_migration_numbers.details: 9 duplicate migration number prefixes found. Migration ordering is non-deterministic for these pairs.
check_6_conflicting_migration_numbers.recommendation: Renumber conflicting migrations to unique sequential prefixes. Non-deterministic ordering can cause schema drift between environments.

check_7_floating_point_money.details: No FLOAT, REAL, or DOUBLE PRECISION found on any money-related columns in migrations. Only false positive hits from comments/strings.

check_8_money_column_precision.details: Initial migrations defined some money columns as bare NUMERIC (without precision), but migration 121_money_column_precision.sql retroactively ALTERs all affected columns (journal_entry_lines.debit/credit, statement_lines.amount, recon_items.amount, intercompany_reconciliation_results.*, budget_version_lines.amount) to NUMERIC(20,2). All post-121 migrations use explicit precision. Newer tables (095_general_ledger, 099_tenant_close_issues, 102_tenant_period_reconciliations) define NUMERIC(20,2) from creation.
check_8_money_column_precision.note: match_confidence in recon_match_groups uses bare NUMERIC which is acceptable since it is a percentage (0-1), not a money column.

check_11_tenant_id_coverage.details: Several tables lack tenant_id column. Some are justifiable (shared/global tables), others are concerning.

acceptable.reason: Global singleton lock table, not tenant-scoped by design
Global taxonomy reference data, shared across tenants
System-level job queue, scoped by close_session_id which links to tenant

concerning.reason: File is named 'tenant_' but table may lack tenant_id. If these are tenant-scoped, this is a tenant isolation gap.

concerning.table: recon_runs, recon_items, recon_match_groups, recon_match_group_items, recon_exceptions, recon_signoffs
concerning.reason: These 6 tables lack tenant_id. They are scoped via close_session_id FK, which links to a tenant indirectly. However, direct tenant_id is recommended for RLS and query isolation.
Named 'tenant_' but lacks tenant_id. Scoped via close_session_id indirectly.
No tenant_id. Scoped via close_session_id. Direct tenant_id recommended for RLS.

check_11_tenant_id_coverage.recommendation: Add tenant_id to recon_runs, recon_items, statement_packages, close_checklist_items tables and enforce via RLS. Indirect scoping via close_session_id is fragile if session IDs are guessable.

check_12_route_file_inventory.details: Found route files organized in 4 directories:

routeFiles.src/routes/close/: 46 route files covering all close workflow sub-routes

check_13_authentication_middleware.details: Auth is applied globally at the server.ts level. Line 134-138 of server.ts applies requireAuth (or optionalAuth in dev mode), attachTenantPool, and requireTenantContext to ALL /api/* routes. Auth routes (/api/auth) are mounted separately above this middleware chain (line 110) and are correctly excluded. The auth pattern is defense-in-depth: global middleware + individual route guards where needed.

check_14_role_based_access.details: requireRole is only used on settings_team.ts (admin-only for role changes, deactivation, deletion) and tenants.ts (admin-only for tenant creation). However, sensitive close operations (certify, lock, advance) do NOT use requireRole middleware.
gapDetails: POST /close/sessions/:id/certify - uses getCloseRoleFromReq() for in-handler checks but no middleware guard
Verification routes (certification artifacts) - no role check; anyone with a valid token can access
check_14_role_based_access.recommendation: The in-handler role checking pattern works but is less robust than middleware guards. Consider adding requireRole middleware for certify/lock operations as a defense-in-depth measure.

check_15_sql_injection.details: All template literal SQL queries use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, etc.). Dynamic query building in repositories (deferred_tax_repository, segment_repository, stock_compensation_repository, audit_ledger_repository) constructs WHERE clauses and SET clauses using parameterized indexes ($${idx}). Column names in SET clauses are hardcoded strings from whitelist properties, not from user input. No raw string concatenation of user input into SQL detected.
check_15_sql_injection.note: db/index.ts line 52 uses template literal for SET search_path but the value (CORE_SEARCH_PATH) is a compile-time constant, not user input. reset_and_bootstrap.ts uses template literals with table names from pg_catalog queries, but this is a dev-only utility script.

check_16_input_validation.details: 17 route files use validateBody with Zod schemas. However, many POST/PUT routes across close/* lack explicit validation middleware.
routesWithValidation: audit_auditor.ts, audit_binder.ts, audit_gaap_policy.ts, audit_pbc.ts, audit_prior_period.ts, audit_professional_review.ts, audit_reconciliation.ts, audit_todos.ts
routesMissingValidation: close_stock_compensation.ts - POST/PUT operations likely lack validateBody
close_journal_entries.ts - POST operations may lack validateBody
check_16_input_validation.recommendation: Add Zod schema validation to all POST/PUT/PATCH routes that accept request bodies. Missing validation allows malformed data to reach the database layer.

check_17_unauthenticated_routes.details: All routes under /api/* are protected by the global auth middleware (server.ts:134). Only /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register are correctly excluded. /health and /readiness endpoints are mounted before the auth middleware and are public by design. In dev mode, optionalAuth is used instead of requireAuth, which is acceptable for development.

issues: Entity encoding bypass via regex injection in DOCTYPE entity names (GHSA-m7jm-9gc2-mpf2)
DoS through entity expansion in DOCTYPE (GHSA-jmr7-xgp7-cmfj)

vulnerabilities.note: xlsx is used in 5 route files (close_excel_export, close_gl_replace, close_journal_entries, gl/ingest, trial-balance/parser). No fix available upstream.

check_18_npm_audit.recommendation: Run 'npm audit fix' to resolve fast-xml-parser and qs vulnerabilities. For xlsx, evaluate switching to the maintained 'exceljs' or 'xlsx-populate' package, as SheetJS has known unfixed vulnerabilities and a restrictive license.

check_19_deprecated_packages.details: xlsx (SheetJS) is effectively abandoned/restrictively licensed. No other obviously deprecated packages found in dependencies. All major packages (express, pg, zod, jsonwebtoken, helmet) are current.
check_19_deprecated_packages.recommendation: Replace xlsx with exceljs for Excel file handling.

check_20_bcryptjs.details: package.json correctly uses 'bcryptjs' (^3.0.3) as a production dependency and '@types/bcryptjs' (^2.4.6) in devDependencies. This is the pure-JS implementation that avoids native module compilation issues on Alpine/Docker.
